However the hold fails the group-relative standard. saturation_screen.json (deviation 0.5, grouped on coloring) gives deep_jewel 43 items, median 0.1628, min 0.1107, outlier_count 0. Reproducing that metric per item puts case_237 at 0.1751 (per-seed 0.1655/0.1909/0.1690) against a group median of 0.1682 - 1.04x its own group median, rank 26 of 43, ABOVE the median, not below it. Further, a visible gem hue in dark regions occurs only in the angular_precise contour sub-family (12 of 43 deep_jewel items); the group median for jewel-hue fraction among dark pixels is 0.0000, and every rounded_soft, broken_dry, selective_edge and crisp_uniform deep_jewel item scores 0.0000, case_237 included. Accepted rounded_soft peers are visually indistinguishable in the disputed respect: P7000703 (sat 0.1763, just above case_237) and P7000715 (sat 0.1976, the highest-saturation rounded_soft deep_jewel item) both render fully achromatic black garments with no gem hue, while P7000007 (angular_precise) is the contrast case that does show a deep emerald blazer. So the achromatic dark garment is the deep_jewel x non-angular family norm, not a case_237-specific failure, and this item sits above its own palette group's median saturation. Any concern about deep_jewel only reading as a gem hue under angular_precise contours is an axis-level palette/contour interaction worth a separate pass across the 31 non-angular deep_jewel items, not a hold on case_237.
